text: Here is a mistake that comes from knowing this lesson well, on the card. In June 2016, Paper 22 asked why glycogen branching enzyme is needed in addition to glycogen synthase. Read this answer. Look at what this answer says about glycogen branching enzyme in particular. It mentions branches, but does not identify the bond. Lowering activation energy is true of enzymes generally; forming branches is this enzyme's role. Naming the particular bond is one way to make this answer precise. This can feel like a useful answer because it is the sentence they have just learnt, and it is not false. But the question was about this enzyme's precise job, and the examiners' comment says the common mistake was being too general rather than stating the type of bond this enzyme catalyses. Glycogen is branched because of alpha one-six glycosidic bonds, from the carbohydrate lessons, and those are what this enzyme makes. So the credited answer names the bond: it catalyses the formation of alpha one-six glycosidic bonds. Now the boundary: that is a ruling about that question. Where a question asks for the mode of action of an enzyme, lowering activation energy can be a marking point; June 2024 credited it for laccase. Keep the sentence; make sure it answers the question in front of you.
